item.text: {"question_id":"4B.4","answer":"No. Although the formal framework described independent courts, binding constitutional judgments, local-government autonomy, parliamentary safeguards, and complaint mechanisms, these were largely reported as legal arrangements rather than demonstrated protection by Sisi when institutions constrained executive power (BATCH-0024-R01-E006; BATCH-0024-R01-E007; BATCH-0024-R01-E010; BATCH-0024-R01-E016). The contrary evidence is substantial: constitutional amendments authorized presidential appointment of heads of judicial bodies and the prosecutor; courts were reported as executive-influenced; military courts retained broad jurisdiction over civilians; and emergency proceedings restricted private lawyer access, case-file access, public hearings, physical appearance before judges, ordinary appeal, and meaningful judicial review. In those emergency proceedings, only the president could authorize, quash, commute sentences, or order a retrial (BATCH-0011-E016; BATCH-0002-E008; BATCH-0008-E025; BATCH-0006-E017; BATCH-0007-E006; BATCH-0007-E009; BATCH-0009-R07-E008). Remote detention-renewal hearings and the reported use of “rotation” further weakened the practical effect of release orders, although the evidence does not establish a complete count or a personal presidential decision in every case (BATCH-0009-R07-E008; BATCH-0006-E017). The NTRA’s fine against Telecom Egypt shows some episodic regulatory enforcement, but its subordination to the communications ministry and security-linked board composition do not establish broader institutional independence (BATCH-0002-E035).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-R01-E006","BATCH-0024-R01-E007","BATCH-0024-R01-E010","BATCH-0024-R01-E016","BATCH-0002-E035"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E016","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0008-E025","BATCH-0006-E017","BATCH-0007-E006","BATCH-0007-E009","BATCH-0009-R07-E008"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal safeguards and some institutional arrangements are described by government or constitutional sources and do not establish de facto independence, funding protection, or compliance with adverse decisions.","Several adverse findings concern accumulated institutional conditions or practices beginning before 2023, though they remained operative or were documented during the target period.","The evidence does not provide a complete census of affected detainees, adverse decisions, executive noncompliance, or the ruler’s personal involvement in each proceeding.","The NTRA enforcement actions do not establish independence of the regulator or broader independence of auditors, legislatures, election bodies, or local governments."],"corrections_made":["Removed the characterization of historical administrative-court rulings as favorable evidence of Sisi’s 2023 protection of checks.","Added the loss of physical judicial appearance, private lawyer communication, case-file access, public hearings, ordinary appeal, and the president’s formal authority over emergency-court sentences.","Preserved the limited formal and episodic institutional evidence without treating it as proof of ruler-attributed protection.","Qualified attribution where the evidence describes authorities or institutional arrangements rather than a personal presidential act."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
